content.title: What is a Stack?
content.description: A Stack is a linear data structure that follows the Last In First Out (LIFO) principle, where the last inserted element is the first one to be removed.

content.content: Stacks are widely used in software development and computer science. They help manage function calls, recursion, browser navigation, text editor undo operations, expression evaluation, and many interview problems.

content.title: Key Principle
content.content: Stack follows the LIFO (Last In First Out) rule. The most recently added element is removed first.

content.title: Stack of Plates
content.content: Imagine a stack of plates in a cafeteria. You place new plates on top and remove plates from the top. The last plate placed is the first plate removed. This is exactly how a Stack works.
The defining characteristic of a Stack is the Last In First Out principle. Every insertion and deletion occurs only at the top of the stack.

content.title: Important Observation
content.description: Elements can only be accessed from the top. Direct access to middle elements is not allowed.

items.question: Push
items.answer: Insert a new element at the top of the stack.

items.question: Pop
items.answer: Remove the top element from the stack.

items.question: Peek / Top
items.answer: View the top element without removing it.

items.question: isEmpty
items.answer: Check whether the stack contains any elements.

items.question: Size
items.answer: Return the total number of elements.

content.content: Push inserts a new element at the top of the stack. The newly inserted element becomes the current top.
Pop removes the top element from the stack and returns it.
Peek (or Top) returns the element currently present at the top of the stack without removing it.
Stacks can be implemented using arrays or linked lists. Both implementations support efficient insertion and deletion at the top.
Two common errors occur while working with stacks: Overflow and Underflow.

items.question: Stack Overflow
items.answer: Occurs when inserting into a full stack.

items.question: Stack Underflow
items.answer: Occurs when removing from an empty stack.

content.title: Important
content.content: Always check whether a stack is empty before performing a pop operation.

items.question: Browser History
items.answer: Back button functionality uses a stack.

items.question: Undo Operations
items.answer: Text editors maintain previous actions in a stack.

items.question: Function Calls
items.answer: Programming languages use a call stack.

items.question: Expression Evaluation
items.answer: Used in postfix and infix calculations.

items.question: Recursion
items.answer: Recursive calls are stored on the call stack.

content.title: Interesting Fact
content.content: Every program you execute uses a stack internally to manage function calls and local variables.

items.question: Valid Parentheses
items.answer: Check matching brackets using a stack.

items.question: Min Stack
items.answer: Design a stack supporting minimum retrieval.

content.title: Interview Insight
content.description: Whenever you see nested structures, matching brackets, undo operations, recursion, or expression evaluation, think about using a Stack.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Overflow occurs when stack is full.
Underflow occurs when stack is empty.
Stacks are used in recursion and function calls.
Push and Pop both work in O(1) time.
